::: {.solutions}

**Show all your reasoning.** Total: **65 marks** · Suggested time: **85 minutes**. You are not meant to
*recognise* these curves — you are meant to **read** them with the fixed checklist (ends · symmetry · sign of
the leading constant · where the wiggles bunch up · turning points).

| Section | What it covers | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Reading unfamiliar curves** | $a\sin(x^{b})$ parameters · even/odd · bounded humps · $\lvert x\rvert$ inside · self-powers | 18 |
| **B — Counting as intersections** | line/curve crossings · $\lvert f\rvert$ counts · cubic-level sets · tangency | 20 |
| **C — Sketching harder curves** | reciprocals of quadratics · exp/log humps · non-function curves · oblique asymptotes · double reflections | 27 |

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Answer form.** Sketches → label every **asymptote, turning point and axis intercept**, and state the
**domain** and any **symmetry** (even/odd). "How many solutions" → **a whole number**, justified by a sketch.
Exact coordinates for maxima/minima.
:::

# Section A — Reading unfamiliar curves

## Question 1 **[4]**

A graph of $y=a\sin(x^{b})$, with $a,b$ non-zero integers, is **odd**, oscillates **infinitely fast near
$x=0$**, flattens towards $0$ as $\lvert x\rvert\to\infty$, and on the right approaches the $x$-axis **from
below**. State everything you can about $a$ and $b$, with reasons.
